Pakistan National Store — Launching a Luxury Bronze Sculpture Brand to International Buyers
How we built a Shopify store capable of selling $5,500–$17,000 handcrafted bronze sculptures to international buyers who had never seen the pieces in person.

Pakistan National Store is the ecommerce arm of Ahmed & Sons Group LLC, operating out of St. Petersburg, Florida. The brand manufactures and imports museum-quality handcrafted bronze sculptures produced by Pakistani master artisans — pieces finished in antique brass, copper, silver, and gold, and priced from $5,500 to $17,000. Target buyers are affluent US and international purchasers: art collectors, interior designers, and corporate gift buyers. The brand entered the engagement with no digital infrastructure and no prior online sales record.

PNS had museum-grade product — a Royal Arabian Stallion at $7,500, Royal Cheetah Companions at $8,500, bronze eagles finished in antique gold — and no digital presence capable of selling it. The challenge was not the product; it was the credibility gap. A buyer spending $7,500 on a sculpture they have never seen in person needs the store to function as a gallery and a sales consultant simultaneously. A standard Shopify template does not do that work. Zero online revenue, zero international sales channel, and zero brand credibility in the digital space were the starting conditions.

Revenue figures are not disclosed at client request. This case study covers the build and launch phase. The store launched in 2024 and is in active operation. Results reflect the infrastructure delivered, not a tracked sales period.

We came in with world-class product and no way to show it to the world. Hydra Fox built us the platform we needed — a store that makes buyers feel the quality before the piece ever ships. The international launch is everything we hoped it would be.

The next phase is driving qualified international traffic to the catalog. Paid search is the priority channel — high-intent buyers searching for luxury bronze sculptures, art collectors researching statement pieces, interior designers sourcing for residential and hospitality projects. Meta prospecting will follow once enough buyer data exists to build reliable lookalike audiences. Email infrastructure is in place; the focus shifts to list-building from product page visitors and abandoned sessions — users who spent significant time on a $7,500 product page are a warm segment worth recovering. A B2B outreach sequence for interior designers and real estate staging companies is scoped but not yet live.

## Store Design & Brand Architecture

PNS sells pieces that compete with gallery sculpture — $7,500 Royal Arabian Stallions,
$8,500 Royal Cheetah Companions, bronze eagles finished in antique gold. At these price
points, the store itself is part of the product. We designed a Shopify experience built
around the brand's core promise: museum-quality craftsmanship, delivered to your home.

The collection architecture was mapped to reflect the brand's range — **Royal Collection**
for flagship prestige pieces, **Ahd-e-Qadeem** for heritage-inspired work, **Mount King**
for animal sculptures, and **New Arrivals** to maintain recency signals and give repeat
visitors a reason to return.

## Luxury UX for High-Ticket Items

Standard ecommerce UX is engineered for impulse — speed, brevity, friction removal.
Luxury ecommerce has different requirements. Buyers spending $7,500–$17,000 need time,
detail, and confidence. We structured every product page around three conversion levers:

- **Material specificity** — antique brass, antique copper, antique silver, antique gold
  finishes described with precision, giving buyers a vocabulary to feel informed
- **Scale and placement** — photography and copy help buyers visualise the piece in their
  own space, critical when the item cannot be seen in a showroom first
- **Policy clarity** — the 7-day exchange policy surfaced early to reduce purchase anxiety
  at this price tier

## International E-commerce Infrastructure

PNS's core ambition is the US market with international expansion beyond it.
We built the checkout, shipping logic, and currency handling to serve this from day one —
the store launched globally rather than building domestic-first and retrofitting later.
Ahmed & Sons Group LLC operates out of St. Petersburg, Florida, which anchors the brand
in the US market while the product's Pakistani artisan origin becomes a differentiator
rather than a barrier.

## Collection Strategy & Merchandising

Across four collections, we structured product naming and merchandising hierarchy to
communicate prestige without alienating first-time visitors. The Royal Collection leads —
positioning the highest-value pieces as the brand's signature. Ahd-e-Qadeem grounds the
brand in heritage and craftsmanship storytelling. New Arrivals gives the catalog motion,
encouraging repeat visits in an otherwise static luxury product category.

## Digital Launch Foundation

The store launched with the infrastructure to support paid media and organic growth:
structured product data, clean URL architecture, SEO-ready metadata across all collections,
and an enquiry path that routes international buyers efficiently. The foundation is built
to scale into paid search and Meta advertising as the brand grows its international footprint.
